draftA:
REQ-1: Compute debt-to-income (DTI) as (all existing monthly debt payments + the new loan's monthly payment) divided by gross monthly income. DTI passes only if it is at most 43%.
REQ-2: Credit score passes only if it is at least 640.
REQ-3: Use only DTI and credit score in v1. No other factor may affect the result. The check must return a result within seconds; the requester should confirm an exact time limit, since none was given.
REQ-4: Show 'likely to qualify' only if both checks pass. Otherwise, show each failed reason in plain words and state that this is not a final decision.
AC-1: Gross income $5,000/month, existing debt $1,500/month, new payment $650/month, score 640. DTI is 2,150/5,000 = 43.0%, so it passes at the limit. Score 640 passes at the limit. The app shows 'likely to qualify'.
AC-2: Same as AC-1, but the new payment is $700. DTI is 2,200/5,000 = 44.0%, above 43%. The app shows 'not likely to qualify' with the reason 'Your monthly debt including this loan would be 44% of your gross income; the limit is 43%', plus 'This is not a final decision'.
AC-3: Same as AC-1, but the score is 639. DTI is 43.0%, so it passes. The score fails because 639 is below 640. The app shows 'not likely to qualify' with the reason 'Your credit score is below the minimum of 640', plus 'This is not a final decision'.
AC-4: Gross income $5,000, existing debt $1,500, new payment $700, score 600. Both checks fail (44.0% DTI; 600 below 640). The app shows both reasons and 'This is not a final decision'.
draftB:
REQ-1: Before a full application, tell the applicant in seconds if they are likely to qualify, and why, only when both rules below pass.
REQ-2: Total monthly debt, including the new loan payment, must be at most 43 percent of gross monthly income.
REQ-3: Credit score must be at least 640, and no other factor may be used in v1.
REQ-4: A decline must give the specific reason in plain words and state that this is not a final decision.
AC-1: Gross monthly income 100, total monthly debt including the new payment 43, score 640: 43 is 43 percent of 100 and 640 meets the minimum, so likely to qualify, with that reason in plain words.
AC-2: Gross monthly income 100, total monthly debt including the new payment 44, score 640: 44 exceeds 43 percent of 100, so decline for debt-to-income over 43 percent, in plain words, and state this is not a final decision.
AC-3: Gross monthly income 100, total monthly debt including the new payment 43, score 639: debt-to-income is at most 43 percent but 639 is below 640, so decline for credit score under 640, in plain words, and state this is not a final decision.

reviewOfA.strengths: The worked examples recompute exactly, and both the 43 percent DTI limit and the 640 score limit are treated as passing.

findings.title: REQ-1 limits answers to passes
findings.detail: As worded, the applicant is told the outcome and reason only when both rules pass. This contradicts the brief, which covers every applicant, and REQ-4, which requires declines to get a reason. Reword so every applicant gets a result and a reason, with likely to qualify only when both rules pass.
findings.quote: tell the applicant in seconds if they are likely to qualify, and why, only when both rules below pass.

findings.title: No test for both rules failing
findings.detail: No acceptance criterion covers an applicant who fails both debt-to-income and credit score, for example debt 44 on income 100 with score 639. The draft does not say whether the decline gives both specific reasons. Add a criterion that lists each failed rule in plain words.
findings.quote: AC-3: Gross monthly income 100, total monthly debt including the new payment 43, score 639

reviewOfB.strengths: The boundary tests are correct and well chosen: 43 of 100 is exactly 43 percent and passes, 44 exceeds it, and 639 falls just below the 640 minimum.

merge.document:
REQ-1: Before a full application, give every applicant a result within seconds: 'likely to qualify' only if both checks below pass, otherwise 'not likely to qualify'. In both cases, say why in plain words. The requester should confirm an exact time limit, since none was given.
REQ-2: Compute debt-to-income (DTI) as (all existing monthly debt payments + the new loan's monthly payment) divided by gross monthly income. DTI passes only if it is at most 43%.
REQ-3: Credit score passes only if it is at least 640. Use only DTI and credit score in v1. No other factor may affect the result.
REQ-4: A decline must give the specific reason for each failed check in plain words and state that this is not a final decision.
AC-1: Gross income $5,000/month, existing debt $1,500/month, new payment $650/month, score 640. DTI is 2,150/5,000 = 43.0%, so it passes at the limit. Score 640 passes at the limit. The app shows 'likely to qualify' with the reason 'Your monthly debt including this loan would be 43% of your gross income, within the 43% limit, and your credit score meets the 640 minimum'.
AC-2: Same as AC-1, but the new payment is $700. DTI is 2,200/5,000 = 44.0%, above 43%. The app shows 'not likely to qualify' with the reason 'Your monthly debt including this loan would be 44% of your gross income; the limit is 43%', plus 'This is not a final decision'.
AC-3: Same as AC-1, but the score is 639. DTI is 43.0%, so it passes. The score fails because 639 is below 640. The app shows 'not likely to qualify' with the reason 'Your credit score is below the minimum of 640', plus 'This is not a final decision'.
AC-4: Gross income $5,000, existing debt $1,500, new payment $700, score 639. Both checks fail (44.0% DTI; 639 below 640). The app shows 'not likely to qualify' with both reasons above in plain words, plus 'This is not a final decision'.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's explicit DTI formula, its dollar-based worked examples, which recompute exactly, its both-checks-fail test, and its note that the requester must confirm an exact time limit.
merge.keptFromB: I kept draft B's framing that the check runs before a full application and explains why to the applicant, including a plain-words reason when they are likely to qualify.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 · P1 · REQ-1 limits answers to passes
resolutions.note: REQ-1 now gives every applicant a result and a plain-words reason within seconds, with 'likely to qualify' only when both checks pass.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 · P2 · No test for both rules failing
resolutions.note: AC-4 covers DTI 44.0% with score 639 and requires both specific reasons plus 'This is not a final decision'. REQ-4 now requires a reason for each failed check.
